text:
Devon: Quick brain-dump — thinking about a 'zipper bundle' handshake for bundles that contain a base weights blob + a set of delta patches. Goal: one manifest-level negotiation instead of per-shard handshakes, atomic apply semantics, and cheaper rollout of small fixes (:thinking:).

Maria: interesting. can you sketch how warmup works with patches? sounds like it could complicate hotstart paths.

Devon: yeah, two main modes i see: overlay-apply (stream patches after base, update KV cache / prefix overlays) vs materialize-rebuild (download base+patches, materialize new bundle then swap). overlay is lower mem but needs careful coherence.

Alex: will this require changing manifest schema? i'd prefer minimal additions to existing registry to keep loaders compatible.

Devon: proposal: manifest has a new "bundle_type":"zipper" and a patches array. sample manifest:
```json
{
  "bundle_version": "1",
  "bundle_type": "zipper",
  "base": "sha256:abcd1234...",
  "patches": [
    {"id":"p-2026-01","scope":"embeddings.*","zip":"p-2026-01.zip","seq":1,"apply":"overlay"},
    {"id":"p-2026-02","scope":"blocks.0-5","zip":"p-2026-02.zip","seq":2,"apply":"overlay"}
  ]
}
```

Sam: nice. what about atomicity? we can't leave runtime in half-patched state if commit fails.

Devon: handshake flow thought:
1) client GET /bundle/<id>/manifest -> returns manifest + compatible shard-map
2) client ensures local base digest matches or fetches base blob stream (supports range requests)
3) client streams patches via /bundle/<id>/patches/<patch_id> and applies them in overlay mode (keeps checksums)
4) client POST /bundle/<id>/commit -> runtime verifies full checksums (base+patches) then does atomic rename/swap of runtime pointers
5) on failure runtime auto-rolls back overlay state or continues serving with fallback base-only model

Alex: add a lease TTL on step 3 so partial downloads can be garbage-collected and other requests can fallback to base-only model. also we need a max-concurrent-patch-downloads to avoid DDOS'ing disk IO.

Maria: warmup implications: overlay mode allows early inference on unaffected layers, but we need per-layer readiness bits in shard metadata so router can route prefix requests appropriately. propose a simple readiness bitmap in the warmup API so routing can decide if it's safe to start low-latency traffic.

Devon: example readiness header returned by runtime:
```
X-Bundle-Readiness: embeddings=ready,blocks.0-5=partial,head=ready
```

Sam: rollback mechanism? if commit fails we should keep a deterministic eviction path for overlay pages. either mark overlay as invalid and evict or keep as quarantined until repair. prefer quarantine + background resync.

Devon: agreed. also need to expose metrics: patch-apply-duration, overlay-memory-bytes, checksum-verify-time, failed-commit-count.

Alex: how about compatibility with safetensors sharded blobs? zipper should not change shard format — patches can be either full-shard replacements or per-tensor deltas inside safetensors chunk. that suggests patch zips might contain small safetensors files mapped to scope-locators.

Maria: for perf experiments, can we prototype with one tenant and a synthetic patch that updates only embeddings? measure end-to-end apply time vs full swap.

Devon: i'll draft an RFC and a small PoC plan:
- manifest extension + handshake spec (simple state machine)
- loader changes: overlay apply, checksums, commit/rollback APIs
- router changes: shard readiness bits + fallback rules
- perf microbench: 6GB base, 300MB patch (embeddings only)
- safety: lease TTLs, max concurrent patches, quarantine + background resync

Sam: +1 to RFC. small note: ensure we don't widen attack surface w.r.t signed manifests — patches must be covered by the manifest signature and patch zips must be signed.

deploy-bot: Link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/zipper-bundles (draft created by Devon)

Maria: also add a section on metrics-driven rollout: if quality/regression monitor flags increased loss during overlay, auto-fallback to base.

Devon: will include. thanks all — i'll post a short RFC tomorrow and tag infra + runtime for comments. :shipit:

Sam: react :thumbsup:
